newsitem.title: USA: Westell Q1 marketing, R&D costs rise.
newsitem.headline: Westell Q1 marketing, R&D costs rise.

text.p: Westell Technologies Inc said Monday it posted an expected increase in its loss from continuing operations in the first quarter ended June 30 due primarily to increases in research and developing and marketing costs.

Those costs increased about $3.4 million in the quarter, primarily to support new product developments, such as the Digital Subscriber Line Access Multiplexer and the Rate Adaptive Digital Subscriber Line, the company said.

Also, there was an increase of about $700,000 in general and administrative costs to handle expanded corporate infrastructure in domestic and international operations and the expenses associated with the move into a new corporate headquarters and manufacturing facility, the company said.
Revenues in the quarter fell to $19.3 million from $20.3 million a year ago, the company said.

This was primarily the result of an expected decline in analog equipment volume, as network providers transition to digital based products, the company said. DSL sales also decreased aabout $600,000 from last year as increased units shipped for trials were at lower average sales prices.
Earlier Thursday, the company reported a loss of $4.5 million, or $0.12 a share, from continuing operations in the quarter, compared to a loss of $1.7 million, or $0.05 a share, a year ago.
Westell shares closed up 3/8 at 18-1/4 Thursday.
